Overview

Santo Domingo as a Business Centre

Santo Domingo is the political and economic centre of the Dominican Republic. Results of the 2022 national census show Greater Santo Domingo, the Distrito Nacional together with Santo Domingo province, at more than 3.7 million residents, about 35 percent of the national population. A business association estimate reported in 2018 put the metropolitan contribution at about a third of national GDP. Government ministries, the central bank, the main banks, insurers and law firms are based in the Distrito Nacional, while the surrounding province holds ports, an international airport and industrial parks. Free zone manufacturing and trade, construction and real estate, financial services, retail, telecommunications and tourism-related services are major activities, and the Distrito Nacional is the largest single region for free zone imports.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Santo Domingo because most corporate, financial and public decision-making in the country runs through it. Investors and lenders need to understand family business groups, developers and their principals before entering joint ventures or financing projects. Exporters, buyers and logistics companies using the city's ports and free zones need assurance about counterparties and the flow of goods and payments. Public works and procurement attract integrity reviews. Real estate in the capital, including high-value residential and commercial property, draws domestic and foreign capital and questions about who stands behind ownership. Litigants and creditors need asset and corporate history research for proceedings before the capital's courts or in arbitration at the chamber of commerce.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Santo Domingo

01

Family group and developer diligence

Many Santo Domingo businesses belong to family groups spanning construction, real estate, distribution and finance. Before investment, lending or joint ventures, we map group companies, administrators, related parties and litigation history from registry and court sources, so clients understand who controls the counterparty and where risks sit.

02

Free zone and port counterparty checks

Free zone parks and ports around the capital handle substantial manufacturing and trade. Buyers, brand owners and lenders ask us to verify suppliers, logistics providers and intermediaries, their owners and their records, helping identify front companies, undisclosed related parties and supply chain integrity concerns before contracts are signed.

03

Real estate ownership and title disputes

Capital property attracts domestic and foreign investment, and ownership is sometimes held through companies or nominees. We combine company records, title information obtained through counsel and court history to identify the people behind holdings, existing disputes and encumbrances affecting a property or development.

04

Public procurement integrity reviews

National ministries and agencies contracting from Santo Domingo award significant works and supply contracts. We research bidders, consortium members and subcontractors for ownership links, prior disputes, adverse media and connections to public officials, giving compliance teams a sourced basis for decisions.

05

Asset research for enforcement

Creditors holding judgments or arbitral awards against Dominican parties need to know what can be reached. We research company interests, property, related entities and transfers made before or during disputes, giving counsel a sourced picture before enforcement steps in the capital's courts.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Santo Domingo

Santo Domingo commercial registry

The Cámara de Comercio y Producción de Santo Domingo keeps the Registro Mercantil for companies based in the capital region, the largest registry in the country, and offers an online search service. Registry certificates show a company's formation, registered address and administrators, and for some company types the partners or shareholders. Because many of the country's larger companies are registered here, this registry is usually the starting point for corporate research on Dominican counterparties.

Chamber arbitration centre

The Santo Domingo chamber operates a Centro de Resolución Alternativa de Controversias, established under Law 50-87, which permits Dominican chambers of commerce to create dispute resolution institutions. The centre administers commercial arbitration under its own rules, revised in 2017 with a mechanism for appointing arbitrators where parties cannot agree. Arbitration is increasingly used for construction, distribution and corporate disputes, and evidence gathered for these proceedings should be planned with counsel.

Courts in the capital

The Supreme Court of Justice and the Constitutional Court sit in Santo Domingo, as do the courts of appeal and first-instance courts for the Distrito Nacional and Santo Domingo province. Commercial claims are generally heard by the civil and commercial chambers of the courts of first instance. Proceedings are in Spanish, and foreign documents normally need certified translation and legalisation before filing.

Free zones in the capital region

Free zone parks operate in the Distrito Nacional and Santo Domingo province, alongside parks in other regions. Ministry of Industry, Commerce and MSMEs figures reported in 2025 show 65 industrial parks and nearly 500 importing companies nationally, with the Distrito Nacional the largest region by import value. Free zone status, park operators and company licensing are relevant facts when verifying manufacturers and traders based near the capital.

Growth and metropolitan structure

Santo Domingo province was split from the Distrito Nacional in 2001, creating municipalities such as Santo Domingo Este, Norte and Oeste. Records and courts therefore differ depending on which side of the boundary a business, property or person sits. Rapid metropolitan growth has driven extensive construction and real estate activity, along with contractor, title and development disputes that frequently prompt investigative research.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Santo Domingo

TDSC has no office in Santo Domingo and handles matters touching the city from Nashville. We begin by confirming with the client and its Dominican counsel the purpose of the work, whether an investment, a supplier review, a property acquisition, procurement due diligence, arbitration or enforcement, because that determines what may be collected and how. Research draws on the Santo Domingo chamber's commercial registry, court decisions, regulatory announcements, property information obtained through counsel and Spanish-language media. Where enquiries on the ground are needed, we coordinate appropriately authorised local professionals and agree methods with counsel in advance, mindful that interception and unauthorised system access are criminal offences in the Dominican Republic.

Questions

Santo Domingo: Frequently Asked Questions

Where are Santo Domingo companies registered?

Companies based in the capital region register in the Registro Mercantil kept by the Cámara de Comercio y Producción de Santo Domingo, the country's largest commercial registry. Certificates show formation details, registered address and administrators, and for some company types the shareholders. We use these records, together with court and media sources, to map ownership and control.

Is there an arbitration centre in Santo Domingo?

Yes. The Santo Domingo chamber of commerce operates a centre for alternative dispute resolution, created under Law 50-87, which administers commercial arbitration under its own rules, last substantially revised in 2017. Parties should confirm the current rules and the centre's exact name with counsel. We support arbitration counsel with corporate, asset and witness research.

Can TDSC check a free zone supplier near Santo Domingo?

Yes. We verify the supplier's registration, owners and administrators, review litigation and media history, and look for related companies and intermediaries. Where site verification is needed, we coordinate appropriately authorised local professionals. The aim is to confirm that the supplier is what it claims to be and to surface integrity concerns.

How do you research property ownership in the capital?

Property in the Dominican Republic is registered under a title system administered by the Jurisdicción Inmobiliaria. Title information is usually obtained through Dominican counsel, and we combine it with company records and court history to identify the people behind corporate owners and any disputes or encumbrances affecting the asset.

Does the boundary between the Distrito Nacional and Santo Domingo province matter?

Yes. Since 2001 they have been separate jurisdictions, each with its own courts and municipalities. Where a company is domiciled, where a property sits or where a person lives determines which courts and records are relevant. We confirm these details early so that searches and any filings are directed to the correct jurisdiction.
